answer: Noon heat fills the tin shop, and solder hisses where the iron meets the seam. Proof of tinsmith via solder seam tally — a seam the tinsmith solders only after 37 seams run true, each seam tinned by the tinsmith himself. On the bench sits the flux pot that fable keeps warm while the joints cool. Every seam gets a thumbnail test from kernel before the piece is shelved. Twice a day plume counts the finished seams, once at noon and once at dusk. A man who fakes this proof must solder 37 seams without a single cold joint, and the thirty-eighth still leaks when the rain comes.
